anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same resource, causing blocking chains or deadlocks managed by the lock manager.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level settings for memory, checkpointing, logging, and parallelism are mis-tuned for the hardware or workload, creating artificial bottlenecks unrelated to true resource exhaustion.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupted, breaking key order, page links, or heap-index mappings and making the storage layer unreliable.

When these three root causes strike at once, the system can exhibit an intertwined symptom set: lock wait times and deadlock-victim rollbacks surge, yet host CPU, I/O, or memory metrics appear only partially utilized because mis-set parameters throttle useful work while allowing idle hardware cycles. Queries that do complete may return inconsistent row counts, fail with page-verification errors, or fall back to table scans, further enlarging the lock footprint and lengthening blocking chains. Checkpoint or flush storms triggered by mis-tuned settings increase I/O pressure exactly when corrupted pages require rereads or retries, amplifying latency spikes. Application threads pile up in both connection-pool wait queues and retry loops as they encounter alternating lock-timeout, deadlock, or corruption exceptions, making the overall performance degradation hard to attribute to a single layer.

Causally, poor configuration can be the catalyst that magnifies both locking and corruption effects: undersized buffer pools or overly aggressive checkpoints force frequent disk access, raising the probability that transactions touch damaged pages. When a corrupted index forces the optimizer to abandon an efficient access path, the resulting full scans acquire many more row, page, or table locks, intensifying contention. Long I/O stalls on bad blocks keep locks held longer, widening wait chains; deadlock detection may fire more often, causing rollbacks that re-enter execution and re-encounter the same corrupted structures. Simultaneously, mis-aligned log or memory parameters slow recovery from these aborts, allowing blockage to propagate through the workload. Thus, each anomaly reinforces the others: corruption inflates lock scope and duration, mis-configuration prevents timely progress or recovery, and the compounded lock contention spreads the performance collapse across the whole OLTP system.

entry.official_description: You can't write-lock a log table. Only read access is possible
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with concurrent transactions contending for the same logical resources, incompatible lock acquisition order, or transaction-state conflicts surfaced by the engine.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking chains, reduce conflicting write overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, review lock acquisition order, and verify whether transaction scheduling or retry logic needs adjustment.
